prompt: An increasing number of students choose to complete their university degree in a foreign country rather than at home. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this trend.
essay:
Studying for a degree overseas has moved from being an unusual choice to being a mainstream one, particularly at postgraduate level. The trend brings real gains to the students who can afford it, but it also carries costs that fall on people other than the student.

For the individual, the advantages are substantial. A foreign university may simply teach a subject better, especially where the home system is under-resourced or where a specialism barely exists locally. Beyond the teaching, a degree taken abroad demands a kind of self-management that a degree taken from a childhood bedroom does not: administrative independence, functioning in a second language every day, and building a social network from nothing. Contacts matter too, since a graduate who has studied in another country leaves with references, acquaintances and a working knowledge of a second job market.

The disadvantages are more easily overlooked because they are not all borne by the student. Cost is the obvious one, and it is not only tuition: international fees are usually set well above domestic rates, and living costs abroad are paid without the family support that keeps domestic study affordable. Less obviously, when the most academically able students of a generation leave and a proportion of them do not return, the countries that educated them to eighteen carry the expense while another country collects the benefit.

Overall, the trend is clearly positive for those able to take part in it, and considerably more ambiguous for the societies they come from. It is worth remembering that access is uneven; a development that helps the students who already had the most options is not the same thing as a development that helps students.
title: Taking a degree in another country
